questions.text:
Acid rain occurs due to nitrogen dioxide in the atmosphere dissolving into rainwater and forming nitrous acid.

One step of this process is shown below:

HNO2(aq) + H2O(l) <=> NO2-(aq) + H3O+(aq)    Kc = 4.50 x 10^-4

Write the equilibrium constant expression for this reaction.
questions.expectedAnswer: Kc = [NO2-][H3O+] / [HNO2]
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct Kc expression.

questions.text:
The value of the equilibrium constant is 1.50 x 10^-2.

Explain what this indicates about the ratio of products and reactants.
questions.expectedAnswer: Kc is the concentration of products divided by the concentration of reactants. Since Kc < 1, the equilibrium lies to the left, meaning reactants are favoured.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: A correct statement about Kc. Merit: Explains the ratio and identifies that the reaction favours reactants.

questions.text:
Industrial emissions have been increasing nitrogen dioxide levels.

Predict the impact on the position of equilibrium as temperature increases, if the enthalpy of this reaction is DrH = +6.80 kJ mol-1.

In your answer:
- describe the effect of temperature on the forward and reverse reactions
- explain any changes that would occur to the value of Kc.
questions.expectedAnswer: The enthalpy is positive, showing the forward reaction is endothermic. Increasing temperature favours the endothermic (forward) direction, producing more products. Kc will increase.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies that increasing temperature will favour the endothermic reaction. Merit: Identifies that the forward reaction is favoured. Excellence: Fully describes the effect on both reactions and Kc.

questions.text: Calculate the pH of a 0.45 mol L-1 solution of hydrochloric acid, HCl.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct value.

questions.text: Calculate the concentration of hydroxide ions, OH-, in a solution of hydrochloric acid, HCl, with a pH of 1.5.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One step correct. Merit: Correct answer with units.

questions.text:
Compare the pH and conductivity of hydrochloric acid, HCl, and nitrous acid, HNO2.

The data for each acid is shown in the table below.

In your answer, include:
- definitions for strong and weak acids
- an explanation of the pH for each solution and relevant equations
- a definition of conductivity
- an explanation for the conductivity of each solution.

graph.title: Comparison of Hydrochloric Acid and Nitrous Acid

questions.expectedAnswer: Strong acids dissociate completely; weak acids dissociate partially. HCl has lower pH because all molecules donate protons. HNO2 has higher pH because only some molecules donate protons. HCl has greater conductivity due to more ions in solution.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies dissociation difference OR defines pH OR defines conductivity. Merit: Explains pH and conductivity for both solutions. Excellence: Justifies both properties with equations.

questions.text:
Pāua are a species of marine sea snail, which form their shells from layers of calcium carbonate, CaCO3, and proteins. The calcium carbonate reacts with acid in the oceans leading to degradation of their shells.

Describe the chemical observations made when the calcium carbonate shells react with acid in the ocean.
questions.expectedAnswer: The shells will slowly lose mass (become thinner), and bubbles will form as CO2 gas is released.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies that mass/thickness will be lost OR bubbles form.

questions.text:
Cross-sectional views of two different pāua shells are shown below.

Pāua Shell A has Total Shell Area = 80 cm2. Pāua Shell B has Total Shell Area = 160 cm2.

Explain which pāua shell is more vulnerable to the effects of ocean acidification.

In your answer, include concepts of:
- collision theory
- rate of reaction.
questions.expectedAnswer: Shell B will be more vulnerable due to having a greater surface area exposed to the acidic water, leading to more frequent collisions between acid particles and the shell surface.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies Shell B as having greater surface area. Merit: Full explanation linking surface area to collision theory and rate.

questions.text:
Pāua use enzymes to help form their shells. Enzymes are biomolecules that act as catalysts for specific reactions.

The graph shows the change in the mass of the pāua shell over time without the use of an enzyme.

Add a second line to the graph to predict the change in mass over time when using the enzyme.
questions.expectedAnswer: Second line shows faster rate (above first line), reaching the same final mass sooner.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Second line shows faster rate.

questions.text:
Discuss how the enzyme affects the rate of the reaction to form pāua shell.

In your answer, refer to:
- the role of a catalyst
- collision theory
- activation energy.
questions.expectedAnswer: Catalysts increase the rate by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy, meaning more particles have sufficient energy for successful collisions.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Basic definition of a catalyst. Merit: Links rate to lower activation energy. Excellence: Full explanation with alternative pathway, activation energy, and successful collisions.

questions.text:
Calcium hydroxide, Ba(OH)2, barium chloride, BaCl2, and barium ethanoate, Ba(CH3COO)2, are soluble calcium compounds.

Write an equation to show the complete dissociation of each of these compounds in water.
questions.expectedAnswer:
Ba(OH)2(s) -> Ca2+(aq) + 2OH-(aq)
BaCl2(s) -> Ca2+(aq) + 2Br-(aq)
Ca(CH3CH2COO)2(s) -> Ca2+(aq) + 2CH3CH2COO-(aq)
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Two correct equations.

questions.text:
Calcium propanoate will react further once dissolved.

Write an equation for the reaction of propanoate, CH3CH2COO-.
questions.expectedAnswer: CH3CH2COO- + H2O <=> CH3CH2COOH + OH-
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies reaction with water. Merit: Correct equation with reversible arrow.

questions.text:
The pH of 0.10 mol L-1 solutions of these three compounds is shown in the graph below.

Discuss the differences in their pH.

In your answer:
- give a definition for acids and bases
- explain how proton transfer is linked to pH
- discuss any ability for these compounds to transfer protons.
questions.expectedAnswer: Acids donate protons; bases accept protons. Ba(OH)2 is strongly basic (OH- accepts protons). BaCl2 is neutral (neither ion transfers protons). Ca(CH3CH2COO)2 is mildly basic (propanoate accepts a proton from water, producing OH-).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises the nature of TWO solutions OR defines acid and base. Merit: Explains how calcium propanoate acts as a basic salt. Excellence: Fully discusses all three.

questions.text:
Phosphorus pentafluoride, PF5, is a potent greenhouse gas. It is produced using phosphorus trifluoride, PF3, and fluorine gas, F2:

PF3(g) + F2(g) <=> PF5(g)

During the manufacturing process, some of the PF5 is removed from the reaction vessel.

Explain, using equilibrium principles, how the system responds to restore equilibrium.
questions.expectedAnswer: Removing the product PF5 will cause the equilibrium to shift forward to replace the lost product.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies forward is favoured. Merit: Correct explanation.

questions.text:
Explain why producing PF5 is favoured when the reaction is transferred to a vessel with a much smaller volume.

In your answer, include:
- a description of the changes occurring
- an explanation of equilibrium principles
- what happens to the position of equilibrium when the pressure is increased.
questions.expectedAnswer: Decreasing the volume increases the pressure. By Le Chatelier's principle, the system shifts to the side with fewer gas moles (forward: 2 moles -> 1 mole), producing more PF5.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Explains why pressure has increased OR identifies forward is favoured. Merit: Identifies pressure favours fewest moles. Excellence: Full explanation with mole comparison.

questions.text:
The equilibrium expression for the reaction is shown below.

Kc = [PF5] / ([PF3][F2])

Calculate the equilibrium constant at 350 degrees C if the concentrations are as follows:
[PF5] = 0.024 mol L-1
[F2] = 0.018 mol L-1
[PF3] = 0.00015 mol L-1
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct value.

questions.text:
Explain the effect of increasing the concentration of F2 on the equilibrium system AND Kc value.

PF3(g) + F2(g) <=> PF5(g)
questions.expectedAnswer: Increasing [F2] favours the forward reaction, producing more PF5 and consuming PF3. Kc does not change because Kc only changes with temperature.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies forward is favoured. Merit: Explains no change to Kc.

questions.text:
The reaction is set up under new conditions, with different temperatures. The data is shown in the table below.

Use the Kc values to explain which set of conditions would increase production of PF5.
questions.expectedAnswer: Condition 1 would be better because Kc = 62 (much greater than 1) means products are strongly favoured at this temperature.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies Condition 1. Merit: Explains why Condition 1 is better.

questions.text: Calculate the concentration of PF3 under each of the new conditions listed in (iii).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One with correct process. Merit: Two concentrations correct.

questions.text:
Fluorine gas, F2(g), can also be used to produce chlorine trifluoride, ClF3(g), a semiconductor manufacturing gas.

3F2(g) + N2(g) <=> 2ClF3(g)

The formation of ClF3(g) is favoured when the temperature is decreased.

Explain why this reaction is performed at 95 degrees C instead of a lower temperature (for example, 25 degrees C).

In your answer:
- identify whether the forward reaction is exothermic or endothermic
- explain any disadvantages of a higher temperature using equilibrium concepts
- explain any advantages of using a higher temperature using collision theory and rate of reaction principles.
questions.expectedAnswer: The forward reaction must be exothermic, as decreasing the temperature favours product formation. Higher temperature disadvantage: shifts equilibrium toward reverse, reducing yield. Higher temperature advantage: increases rate of reaction by increasing frequency and energy of collisions. A compromise temperature of 95 degrees C is used.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies forward reaction as exothermic OR describes faster particle movement. Merit: Explains equilibrium disadvantage AND collision theory advantage. Excellence: Full explanation including the compromise.
